device.category: 6-voice multitimbral analogue BBD-resonator synthesizer (desktop, 19-inch rack or VESA), no keyboard or display
device.based_on: Original design (Belgium, 2026) by Eli Clement, Matthew Philpott and Boris Uytterhaegen; billed as the first analogue BBD synthesizer.

sources.title: Morphor ECHON 6 Owner's Manual, revision 1.2 (April 2026)
sources.note: Features and specifications, voice architecture (exciter, BBD resonator, output), Quad LFO, modulation matrix, voice groups and MIDI channels, settings menu, MIDI implementation with full CC chart and modulation source/destination tables.

architecture.polyphony_mode: 6-voice polyphonic; up to 6 voice groups (multitimbral), each with its own sound, MIDI channel, unison and voice allocation
architecture.patch_memory_note: 216 presets (6 banks x 6 sub-banks x 6), each holding all voice groups; a scratch pad saved at power-off by an internal UPS. MIDI channels and system settings are global.
architecture.summary: Each voice is an exciter feeding a resonator. The exciter is a small subtractive synth: an analogue VCO whose WAVE knob morphs sine, triangle, ramp, 5% pulse and square (or crossfades from the external input), analogue noise through a sample-and-hold, and a DADSR envelope on a VCA. Its output passes a 12 dB/oct low-pass INPUT FILTER into a 1024-stage BBD whose clock always follows the note (NOTE OFFSET, FINE TUNE, GLIDE). FEEDBACK through a 6 dB/oct in-loop filter, optionally inverted, makes the delay resonate like a struck, bowed or blown body, up to self-oscillation. DRY/WET blends exciter and resonator before pan and level. Four LFO + random generators per voice; a dense 9-source x 32-destination modulation matrix.
architecture.synthesis_note: Analogue modal-style synthesis: one BBD resonator (one mode) per voice; unison stacks six into a multi-mode body.

modules.name: MIDI and voice groups
modules.description: Receives MIDI (no keyboard) on a preset channel and up to six voice-group channels; allocates voices per group (five priority modes, unison). The six NUMBER keys can also play voices.

modules.name: External input
modules.description: Mono +4 dBu input, available to each voice group's exciter when enabled; LED white when present, red when clipping.

modules.name: Exciter VCO
modules.description: Analogue VCO, about 16 Hz-4.2 kHz (8 octaves). WAVE morphs sine > triangle > ramp > 5% pulse > square (or ext in > waves). Follows the keyboard only through KEY FOLLOW modulation.

modules.name: Exciter noise
modules.description: Analogue transistor white noise through a sample-and-hold; NOISE S&H RATE tracks COARSE FREQ for most of its range, then rises to continuous white noise.

modules.name: Wave / noise mix
modules.description: Crossfade from VCO (or ext in blend) to noise.

modules.name: Envelope
modules.description: DADSR: onset delay 0-2 s, logarithmic attack, exponential decay and release; short (to ~250 ms), medium or long (to ~25 s) ranges; HOLD, LEGATO, LOOP.

modules.name: Exciter VCA
modules.description: Envelope-controlled amplitude; LEVEL sets how hard the resonator is driven (above about 3 o'clock, sustained signals distort the BBD).

modules.name: Input filter
modules.description: 12 dB/oct low-pass, 32.7 Hz-21 kHz; its output feeds both the BBD and the dry path.

modules.name: Resonator pitch chain
modules.description: MIDI note (and bend) plus NOTE OFFSET (±12 st), FINE TUNE (±3 st) and GLIDE (0-1 s) set the BBD clock; the result is also the KEY FOLLOW source (C0-C8 = 0-1).

modules.name: BBD resonator
modules.description: 1024-stage bucket-brigade delay with pitch-compensated clocking; with feedback it resonates at a pitch set by the clock. Higher clock: tighter, shorter rings; lower: longer sustain.

modules.name: Feedback filter
modules.description: 6 dB/oct low-pass inside the feedback loop: damping, and a lower perceived pitch as it closes.

modules.name: Feedback amount and polarity
modules.description: FEEDBACK level back into the BBD, normal or INVERTed (a different resonant mode); safe up to self-oscillation.

modules.name: Dry / wet
modules.description: Blend of the filtered exciter and the resonator; with a self-oscillating resonator it acts as the resonator's VCA.

modules.name: Voice pan and level
modules.description: Per-voice PANNING (kept on the individual outputs) and voice-group LEVEL.

modules.name: LFO 1
modules.description: Periodic wave (sine, triangle, ramp, square; 20 s to 50 Hz, or 19 MIDI-clock divisions) mixed with a stepped random generator (with smoothing); amplitude, uni/bipolar, KB reset or single-shot.

modules.name: LFO 2
modules.description: Periodic wave (sine, triangle, ramp, square; 20 s to 50 Hz, or 19 MIDI-clock divisions) mixed with a stepped random generator (with smoothing); amplitude, uni/bipolar, KB reset or single-shot.

modules.name: LFO 3
modules.description: Periodic wave (sine, triangle, ramp, square; 20 s to 50 Hz, or 19 MIDI-clock divisions) mixed with a stepped random generator (with smoothing); amplitude, uni/bipolar, KB reset or single-shot.

modules.name: LFO 4
modules.description: Periodic wave (sine, triangle, ramp, square; 20 s to 50 Hz, or 19 MIDI-clock divisions) mixed with a stepped random generator (with smoothing); amplitude, uni/bipolar, KB reset or single-shot.

modules.name: Outputs
modules.description: Main stereo mix (MASTER), headphones (PHONES, independent), and six individual voice outputs; a voice plugged into its individual output leaves the main mix.

connections.note: The resonator always tracks the keyboard.
Pitch bend joins the note in the pitch chain (and so in KEY FOLLOW).
At WAVE minimum the exciter outputs the external input instead of a sine, crossfading into the other waves.
Positive feedback loop; INVERT flips polarity.
Voices patched to their individual outputs leave the main mix.

mod_matrix.name: Modulation matrix (dense)
mod_matrix.note: Every source/destination pair (9 x 32 = 288) has its own depth, polarity and mute, set by holding a SOURCE SELECTION key and turning the destination knob; multiple sources sum on a destination. Each source also passes through its SOURCE MACRO attenuverter (the Quad LFO macro scales all four LFOs). Unipolar sources push from the knob's value, bipolar LFOs swing around it; results clip at the control's range. Over MIDI: CC 109 source, CC 110 destination, CC 111 depth, CC 112 polarity, CC 113 enable. LFOs can cross-modulate each other's rate, mix, amplitude and random rate.

indicators.label: NUMBER LEDs
indicators.function: Active voices, voice groups, preset digits, settings values.

indicators.label: DESTINATION LEDs
indicators.function: Red positive, blue negative; brightness shows depth; blinking when muted.

indicators.label: SOURCE LEDs
indicators.function: Selected source; also an original-value bar while turning a knob.

indicators.label: SELECT and WAVE LEDs
indicators.function: Selected LFO (brightness = amplitude), waveform, polarity (red bipolar, white unipolar), sync blink; MIDI channel display.

indicators.label: EXT IN LED
indicators.function: White when the input is present and enabled, red when clipping.

behaviours.name: Exciter and resonator
behaviours.rule: The exciter (VCO, S&H noise or external input under a DADSR) passes the INPUT FILTER into the BBD and the dry path. With feedback the BBD reinforces frequencies tied to its delay and resonates: short exciter bursts strike it, sustained ones bow or blow it. FEEDBACK past the damping threshold self-oscillates with no input; FEEDBACK FILTER damps the loop and lowers the perceived pitch; INVERT locks onto a different mode. DRY/WET blends exciter and resonance.

behaviours.name: Pitch
behaviours.rule: The resonator always follows the note through NOTE OFFSET, FINE TUNE and GLIDE. The VCO follows only via KEY FOLLOW modulation (full depth in INIT), so exciter and resonator pitch can be detached for beating, moiré and inharmonic textures.

behaviours.name: Envelope modes
behaviours.rule: Short, medium or long ranges; HOLD ignores note-off (NUMBER keys toggle held voices); LEGATO continues from the current level; LOOP repeats onset delay, attack and decay while held.

behaviours.name: Quad LFO
behaviours.rule: Each of four per-voice LFOs mixes a periodic wave with stepped random (optionally smoothed). Free (20 s to 50 Hz) or MIDI-clock synced (19 divisions), uni or bipolar, KB reset or single-shot. RANDOM RATE at zero holds a per-voice random offset.

behaviours.name: Modulation
behaviours.rule: Six source sections (envelope, Quad LFO = four sources, modwheel, velocity, aftertouch, key follow) to 32 destinations per voice in a dense matrix. Hold SOURCE SELECTION and turn a destination knob to assign; DESTINATION button mutes, long press deletes. Detached sources turn their SOURCE MACRO into a manual control. Polyphonic aftertouch works per voice.

behaviours.name: Voice groups
behaviours.rule: A preset holds up to six voice groups, each with its own sound, MIDI channel (default 2-7), unison, priority, bend range and external input setting. Voices are assigned to groups in voice group edit mode. The preset channel (default 1) plays groups by unison (all groups) or by preset priority. CCs on the preset channel edit the group selected with CC 114.

behaviours.name: Presets
behaviours.rule: 216 presets in 6 banks x 6 sub-banks x 6, loaded with PRESET + three NUMBER keys, saved with WRITE. RELOAD compares with the saved version. An internal UPS saves the scratch pad at power-off. Program change: CC 0 (bank) + CC 32 (sub-bank) + PC (slot), or CC 0 + PC 0-35, or PC 0-127 alone (banks 0-3).

behaviours.name: Playing without MIDI
behaviours.rule: In preset mode each NUMBER key plays its voice (middle C, velocity 127 by default; note, velocity, modwheel and aftertouch per key are editable).

behaviours.name: Individual outputs
behaviours.rule: A voice patched to its individual output (stereo TRS, panning kept) leaves the main mix; voice outputs can feed EXT IN for cross-feedback and chained resonators.

midi.note: Every panel control has a CC; the manual's chart lists ranges, accepted channels and whether each is modulatable.

specifications.exciter: analogue VCO (sine, triangle, ramp, pulse, square), analogue S&H noise, external input, DADSR + VCA
specifications.resonator: 1024-stage BBD, 12 dB/oct input LPF, 6 dB/oct feedback LPF, polarity invert
specifications.lfos: 4 per voice (24 total) with random generators
specifications.midi: DIN in, out, thru; USB-C class compliant

not_in_source: envelope times beyond the range end points
exact VCO and BBD clock ranges in Hz beyond the VCO's ~16 Hz-4.2 kHz
source_inconsistencies: In the CC chart, LFO 4's mix, KB reset, single shot, rate, polarity and clock sync (CC 90-95) are labelled 'LFO 3'.
CC 46 FINE TUNE lists 'Short / Medium / Long' values and CC 47 NOTE OFFSET lists 'Off / On', both copied from other rows.
CC 43 FEEDBACK and CC 5 GLIDE are marked not modulatable, but both are matrix destinations (10 and 11); CC 41 INVERT is marked modulatable but is not a destination.
LFO 1 WAVE (CC 49) is marked not modulatable, LFO 2-4 WAVE are marked modulatable; no LFO wave appears in the destination table.
Key features list 'ADSR with onset delay' and 'DADSR'; the envelope is DADSR throughout the manual.
Key features call the WAVE morph a 'blend between 2 VCO waveforms'; the WAVE control text describes a morph through five shapes.
Sustain and release are not modulation destinations (the destination list has onset delay, attack and decay only).

modelling_gaps.detail: Voice modules are modelled once (per_voice); voice groups are described in behaviours.
288 source/destination pairs each hold depth, polarity and mute; modelled as a matrix with 288 slots and no per-slot parameters.
Recorded as physical_modelling: analogue modal-style synthesis with one BBD resonator per voice (see synthesis_note).
Modulation reaches parameters through the matrix (destinations name parameters), so exciter, filter and output modules carry no separate CV input nodes.
